use_case: A developer runs `codex` in their terminal (or IDE/desktop app) and asks it to read, edit, and test code in a local repository: fixing bugs, adding features, running shell commands, and reviewing changes, all in a sandbox with approval prompts.
not_for: Not a GUI or computer-use agent; it works through terminal commands and file patches
Not made for data or SQL analytics, or for non-coding office work
Needs the OpenAI Responses API (a ChatGPT login or API key); other providers need a shim
Commands run in a sandbox, and network access is off by default
evidence: The README (line 1) says: "Codex CLI is a coding agent from OpenAI that runs locally on your computer." The system prompt codex-rs/core/gpt-5.2-codex_prompt.md starts with "running as a coding agent in the Codex CLI" and covers apply_patch edits, git worktree safety, the plan tool, code review, and frontend tasks. Tool handlers in codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/ include shell_spec.rs, unified_exec/exec_command.rs, apply_patch.rs, plan.rs, view_image.rs, mcp.rs, and multi_agents/spawn.rs, and spec_plan.rs adds a hosted web_search tool.
